blocks.task_summary: Find the angle α (0<α<π/2) between a line and a plane, given the line in symmetric form (x−1)/3=(y+2)/2=(z−5)/(−1) and the plane 4x+(cosα)y+(sinα)z=1.
method_path: Extract direction vector d=⟨3,2,−1⟩ from symmetric line equation
Extract normal vector n=⟨4,cosα,sinα⟩ from plane equation
Recognise angle between d and n is π/2−α
Substitute into cos(π/2−α)=d·n/(|d||n|) to obtain 12+2cosα−sinα=√17√14 sinα
accepted_alternatives: Cross-product route: compute |d×n|²=(2sinα+cosα)²+(−4−3sinα)²+(3cosα−8)², substitute into sin(π/2−α)=|d×n|/(|d||n|) to obtain √((2sinα+cosα)²+(4+3sinα)²+(3cosα−8)²)=√17√14 cosα, solve for α≈0.932

normal vector of the plane is (4,cosα,sinα) (seen anywhere) (A1)
recognizing angle between normal and direction vector is π/2−α (seen anywhere) (M1)
attempt to substitute into the formula for the angle between two vectors to form an equation in α (M1); 12+2cosα−sinα=√17√14 sinα
